plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of AeroIQ, focusing on the dashboard's information hierarchy, the drill-down flow to endpoint details, and the alert management workflow.
plan.summary: The run will start by validating the global controls (environment/time filters) on the Dashboard. It will then simulate an incident response workflow: identifying a failing endpoint from the grid, drilling down into its detail view to analyze error samples, and finally navigating to the Alerts center to manage notifications. The Service Map will be checked for navigational utility.
assumptions: The 'Logs', 'Integrations', and 'Settings' links in the sidebar are placeholders (#) and do not lead to functional pages.
The application is a static prototype; data updates may require page reloads or might be simulated via JS interactions.
The 'Service Map' relies on visual node interaction which may behave differently than standard list views.
risk_hotspots: Dashboard: Interaction between Environment tabs (Prod/Staging/Dev) and Time Range selectors.
Endpoint Detail: Readability of the 'Error breakdown' tabs and 'Recent error samples' table.
Alerts Page: Functionality of the multi-select filters (Severity, Status, Assignee).
Mobile Viewport: Sidebar navigation accessibility and tap target sizes (prescan flagged <44px targets).

phases.title: Dashboard Global Controls & Overview
phases.objective: Validate the primary entry point and global context switching.
key_checks: Click through Environment tabs (Production, Staging, Dev) to check for state changes.
Verify visibility and layout of the 4 KPI cards and the Endpoint Health grid.
exit_criteria: All global filters respond to clicks.
KPI cards and Endpoint grid are fully rendered.

phases.title: Incident Drill-Down Flow
phases.objective: Test the core user journey from high-level health to specific error diagnosis.
key_checks: Identify a 'Red' (unhealthy) endpoint card on the Dashboard (e.g., POST /v1/payments).
Click the endpoint card to navigate to `endpoint-detail.html`.
Analyze the Detail view: Check the 6 KPIs, Trend Charts, and Error Breakdown tabs.
Review the 'Recent error samples' table for readability and actionable data.
exit_criteria: Successful navigation from Dashboard to Detail view.
Detail view charts and tables are populated and legible.

phases.title: Alert Management Workflow
phases.objective: Evaluate how users monitor and resolve active incidents.
key_checks: From Dashboard, click 'view all' in the Active Alerts panel or the Alert bell icon.
On `alerts.html`, test the filter bar (Severity, Rule, Assignee, Status).
Attempt to interact with 'Assign' or 'Silence' actions on an alert row.
Check if clicking an alert row links back to the relevant endpoint detail.
exit_criteria: Filters apply correctly to the alert list.

phases.title: Inventory & Topology Exploration
phases.objective: Assess secondary navigation paths for system overview.
key_checks: Navigate to `endpoints.html`: Test sorting/filtering of the full endpoint list.
Navigate to `services.html`: Inspect the Service Map visualization.
Attempt to click a service node on the map to see if it links to details.
exit_criteria: Service map nodes are interactive or clearly informational.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Validate usability on smaller screens, addressing prescan warnings.
key_checks: Verify tap targets for Environment/Time filters (prescan noted <44px height).
Ensure tables (Endpoints/Alerts) handle horizontal overflow gracefully.
exit_criteria: Critical controls are usable despite small touch targets.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 HTML files provided in the site directory.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible filters, tabs, and navigation links. Interact with at least one 'Assign/Silence' action.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 (Dashboard) and Phase 3 (Alerts) checks on mobile viewport to verify layout shifts.

notes: Prescan identified multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings on the top bar filters; pay close attention to these during mobile testing.
The 'Logs' and 'Settings' pages appear to be stubs; do not spend steps attempting to debug them unless they unexpectedly load content.
Focus on the visual hierarchy of the 'Error breakdown' section in the detail view, as this is critical for debugging.
